thread:
Sean Gallagher: hey all — for the known-issues sprint, can Support/Docs drop the **top shortlist** you want SRE to validate? need to sanity check mitigations + make sure we have matching runbooks/alerts before this gets published broadly.

Sean Gallagher: specifically looking for:
- issue title + symptoms (customer-facing)
- affected tier(s)/regions/models
- proposed workaround steps (copy/paste)
- “when to escalate/page” trigger
- owner/reviewer assignment

Sean Gallagher: if you can post 5–8 items w/ links (draft docs ok), we’ll assign reviewers today.

Dev Patel: yep. shortlist we’re targeting for batch 1 (highest ticket volume + most escalation pain):
1) Streaming disconnects/timeouts + reconnect guidance (Hosted) — draft KB: workaround-streaming-timeouts-and-reconnect
2) 429 quota mismatch / rate-limit headers confusing after SDK upgrade (Hosted) — draft KB: workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers
3) Dedicated autoscaling oscillation causing latency spikes (Dedicated) — draft KB: workaround-dedicated-autoscaling-oscillation
4) Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations (Private) — draft KB: workaround-private-installer-upgrade-stuck-migrations
5) Audit log delivery latency (Enterprise/Private) — draft KB: workaround-audit-log-delivery-latency

Dev Patel: all of these will have a “when to escalate” callout + request-id/time-window checklist. still tightening language to avoid customer-specific details.

Priya Shah: +1. also adding a small section in each: “Support verification steps” (what to check in dashboards / what to ask customer for) so we don’t keep pinging on-call for basics.

Rafael Mendes: thanks. quick flag: #2 (429/rate-limit) might be Platform ownership more than SRE. we can still review escalation triggers, but we should have Platform sign off on the technical details.

Mina Haddad: for #2, routing/fallback can make headers look weird in edge cases. we should be careful about claiming “headers always reflect true quota” until ENG-4825 is rolled out everywhere.

Allison Grant: for #5 (audit log lag) I want to ensure we’re consistent on expectations/SLO wording. what are we publishing as “expected delivery”? (and do we have a metric we can point Support to?)

Dev Patel: for #5 we currently say “expected within minutes, may be delayed during backlog; escalate if >30m for enterprise or if customer compliance workflow is blocked.” but open to edits based on your alert thresholds.

Sean Gallagher: perfect. here’s reviewer assignment proposal — please confirm:
- #1 Streaming disconnects/timeouts: **Sean** (SRE) + **Elliot** (Docs) for clarity
- #3 Dedicated autoscaling oscillation: **Rafael** (SRE) + ping capacity folks if needed
- #5 Audit log delivery latency: **Allison** (obs/SLO) + **Rafael** as backup
- #2 429/quota/headers: **Mina** (Platform/routing) + SRE only reviews “when to page”/incident criteria
- #4 Private installer upgrade stuck migrations: this is mostly Platform/Private Deployments — can **Priya N.** assign an eng reviewer on your side?

Priya Natarajan: yep. I’ll route #4 to Private Deployments on-call + ask Ethan to review the escalation path + artifacts checklist. we also need to ensure rollback steps are marked “only w/ engineer guidance” (don’t want Support accidentally walking someone into data loss).

Owen Phillips: re: “when to escalate” wording — can we align to the new playbook language? ex:
- page owning on-call for P0 immediately
- for P1: page if multi-tenant/regional suspected OR no credible mitigation plan in 30 min
and make sure each KB article includes *which* on-call (SRE vs Platform vs Runtime).

Sean Gallagher: +1. also please add a line in each workaround: “If customer reports multiple accounts/regions impacted, move to #incidents and start bridge.” (keeps us out of long DM escalations)

Elliot Price: Docs side: can everyone reviewing please focus on:
- removing any customer names / account identifiers
- avoiding definitive root cause unless we’re confident
- making workarounds “safe-by-default” (no risky toggles without warnings)

Allison Grant: for #5 I’ll propose concrete triggers that match what we can actually see:
- if lag metric (once available) > X for Y mins => page
- until metric is live: Support checks pipeline backlog dashboard + asks for sample event timestamps
I’ll send edits inline once I see the draft.

Dev Patel: works. I’ll drop the draft links in a single comment + tag each reviewer. target: EOD today so we can publish early next week.

Rafael Mendes: please include runbook links (even if internal) in the “Support verification steps” section. we can keep internal-only links in a separate block if needed.

Sean Gallagher: cool. once we review, we’ll confirm whether each one needs a runbook update / alert tweak (esp audit log + streaming) vs just doc changes.

Dev Patel: ack. posting links now + will add a column in the triage sheet for “SRE validated (Y/N)” so we don’t publish prematurely.
